name: Albuterol (Salbutamol)

card.summary: The standard asthma rescue inhaler; its use for fat loss or muscle is limited to scattered bodybuilder use and small lean-mass studies of oral dosing.
card.note: Prescription asthma drug; beta-2 agonists are regulated in sport.

quick.overview:
Albuterol (salbutamol) is a short-acting beta-2 agonist used as a rescue bronchodilator for asthma and COPD. It is among the most prescribed medicines in the US.

Wikipedia notes that some recreational bodybuilders use albuterol and other beta-2 agonists, and that oral use has been studied for muscle wasting and obesity, with human studies reporting more lean mass and less fat mass. The sources reviewed contain no trials in healthy people seeking cosmetic changes.
quick.mechanism: It activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, raising cAMP, which relaxes airway smooth muscle; the same receptor class is involved in lipolysis and muscle effects.
quick.risks: Common effects are tremor, anxiety, headache, cramps, dry mouth and palpitations; higher doses can cause tachycardia, arrhythmia and low potassium. Asthma research has examined links between heavy beta-agonist use and asthma death. It is prescription-only in the US, UK and Canada.

lead: Albuterol, known as salbutamol outside the US, is a short-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist sold as Ventolin, ProAir and Proventil, among others. It is a first-line rescue bronchodilator for bronchospasm in asthma and COPD. [1][3][4]
It was discovered in 1966 by a team led by David Jack at Allen & Hanburys, launched in the UK in 1969 as Ventolin and approved in the US in 1982. [4]

Its place in appearance discussion rests on its being a beta-2 agonist: Wikipedia reports use by some recreational bodybuilders and small studies of oral dosing for lean mass. [4] Published trials of its use for cosmetic fat loss or muscle in healthy people were not identified in the reviewed sources.

paras: Albuterol treats bronchospasm in asthma, including exercise-induced, and in COPD, and is a standard rescue medication in asthma guidelines. [1][4] Other medical uses include acute hyperkalemia; intravenous use to delay preterm labour has largely been replaced by nifedipine. [4]

Wikipedia states some recreational bodybuilders use albuterol and other beta-2 agonists, and that oral use has been studied as an anti-obesity and anti-muscle-wasting approach, with human studies showing increased lean mass, reduced fat mass and lipolysis. It does not describe off-label weight-loss use as common. [4]

Common effects are fine tremor, anxiety, headache, muscle cramps, dry mouth and palpitations. Tachycardia, arrhythmia and flushing can occur, rarely myocardial ischemia, and high or prolonged doses may cause hypokalemia. [4]
A 1992 Canadian case-control study examined whether regular beta-2 agonist use was associated with death or near death from asthma. [2]

A tertiary butyl group makes it selective for beta-2 receptors, which predominate on bronchial smooth muscle. Receptor activation raises cAMP and lowers intracellular calcium, relaxing the muscle. [4]

Inhaled salbutamol was banned at the 1972 Olympics but permitted by 1986; current WADA rules allow inhaled use up to 1600 micrograms over 24 hours, and as of 2011 there was no evidence that inhaled salbutamol improves performance, although oral or intravenous use has been reported to help. [4] It is on the WHO Essential Medicines List and is prescription-only in the US, UK and Canada. [4]

No studies found testing albuterol for cosmetic fat loss or muscle gain in healthy people. Wikipedia cites human studies of oral beta-2 agonist use in obesity and muscle wasting that reported increased lean mass and reduced fat mass. [4] Asthma guidelines and trials establish its use as a rescue bronchodilator. [1]

timeline.event: Discovered at Allen & Hanburys by a team led by David Jack. [4]
Launched in the UK as Ventolin. [4]
Approved for medical use in the US. [4]
